senses.gloss:
तट् तट्, cl. 1. P. तटति, &c., to rumble,
groan; to be raised or elevated, rise; cl. 10.
P. ताटयति, to beat, strike; (a various reading for
तड्); [cf. Lith. tesiu, ‘to raise.’]

तट, अस्, आ, m. f. a slope, an acclivity, declivity,
precipice; the sky or horizon (as appearing to slope);
(अस्, आ or ई, अम्), m. f. n. a shore or bank; a term
applied to certain parts of the human body which
have, as it were, sloping sides (e. g. श्रोणि-तट,
स्तन-तट, q. v.); (अम्), n. a field; [cf. अ-तट,
उत्-तट, पुर-तटी.]
—तट-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, situ-
ated on a declivity, or on a bank or shore; standing
near; indifferent, not partaking of or engaging in,
alien, neuter; (अस्), m. an indifferent person, one
neither a friend nor a foe; (अम्), n. that property
which is distinct from the nature of anything and yet
is the faculty by which it is known, spiritual essence
unconnected with bodily wants or passions.
तटक, अम्, n. a shore or bank.

तटाक, अस्, अम्, m. n. a pond deep enough for
the lotus and other aquatic flowers.

तटिनी, f. a river (as having a bank).
—तटिनी-
पति, इस्, m. ‘the lord of the rivers,’ the ocean.

तट्य, अस्, आ, अम्, living on hills or slopes,
epithet of Śiva.

तटतट तटतट (an onomatopoetic word to
express a particular noise), rumbling, thundering, &c.

ताटङ्क ताटङ्क, अस्, m. an ornament for
the ear, a large sort of ear-ring; [cf. ताडङ्क.]

ताटस्थ्य ताटस्थ्य, अम्, n. (fr. तट-स्थ, a
by-stander), proximity; indifference, disregard, ex-
emption from attachment or aversion, neutrality.

तटाघात (˚ट-आघ्˚), अस्, m. = वप्र-क्रीडा,
the butting of elephants against banks, &c.
